I don’t buy this. 

Yes, the charitable read is that constant attacking/defending leads to an overall more hardened structure. I think everyone can feel how that makes intuitive sense. 

But, I’d draw an analogy between this and Kelly betting. Everyone knows you don’t want to make repeated bets with full risk of ruin. The problem with cybersecurity and cryptocurrency is that due to the irreversible nature of transactions, you’re always in a ”risk of ruin”-like environment. If you have an automated warfare cybersecurity environment, I’d wager that your risk of ruin is actually higher, even if the ”probability of penetration per attempt” is lower. 

The fact that every possible exploit at every protocol at all times is constantly attempted… across the whole stack, at every layer… like, it’s possible that some Lindy applications like the Bitcoin baselayer would be more secure in this way. 11. Amazon $AMZN is reportedly working to reduce its reliance on Anthropic's AI models as the cost of operating Alexa+ continues to climb, according to Business Insider. Internal projections estimated that Alexa+ cloud computing expenses could reach approximately $1.7B in 2026, nearly triple the prior year's costs, prompting Amazon to explore routing more AI requests through its own lower-cost models and infrastructure. The company also considered delaying or scaling back Moonraker, its advanced AI agent initiative, which was projected to require more than $100M in GPU spending this year. The developments highlight the growing pressure on major technology companies to improve AI inference economics, reduce dependence on third-party model providers, and balance increasingly expensive AI capabilities with sustainable profitability.

12. The equal-weight index has gained 4.3% this month, compared with just 0.3% for the S&P 500, marking a sharp reversal from September, when equal-weight stocks underperformed by 4.7 percentage points, their worst relative month since March 2020. For comparison, the equal-weight index outperformed by 4.2 percentage points in April. Year-to-date, the Equal-Weight Index is up 13.4% versus 12.1% for the S&P 500, suggesting market leadership is broadening beyond the largest technology and AI companies as more sectors and individual stocks participate in the rally.
